Add boundary contracts (B12): a Spring Boot module's routes, listeners, schedules, bean definitions and configuration keys, the advice on each bean, and the places where an annotation does not do what it says, read from the class files (verification pending)

Record session traces

Add validation checks to boundary contracts: the constraints inside a wire type's properties, and ! lines for a nested type no @Valid leads into, a body taken without @Valid, a group a @Valid or @Validated leaves out and a constraint on a type its validator cannot handle (verification pending)

Add the activation block to boundary contracts: what switches each kind of annotation on (an @Enable annotation on a configuration in scope, an auto-configuration whose conditions hold, a Bean Validation provider), with a ! line for a family nothing enables (verification pending)

Add the stored types block to boundary contracts: the shape of each Spring Data MongoDB document as the mapper stores it, and a ! line for every query, update, index, sort, projection or @Query string that names a field the document does not have (verification pending)

Add reach lines to boundary contracts: under each entry point what it reads, writes, sends, calls and publishes, from a call graph over the application's own classes, with a ! line for a GET with side effects and a read-only transaction that writes (verification pending)

Place each reach effect with respect to transactions: a send or an HTTP call from inside a transaction (a dual write), an event published outside one that a @TransactionalEventListener waits for, and an after-commit listener that writes are ! lines (verification pending)

Add request binding checks to boundary contracts: a @PathVariable whose name is a variable of no template of its route, a binder whose parameter name the compiler did not record, a required = false binder on a primitive, two @RequestBody parameters, and two handlers on one route are ! lines (verification pending)

Add throws lines to boundary contracts: under each route what it throws and what each exception becomes (the @ExceptionHandler that takes it and its status, a @ResponseStatus, a ResponseStatusException's status, or a 500), with ! lines for an exception of the module's own that nothing maps and for two handlers of one type in one advice (verification pending)
